reason: Start developing the local routing rule using the practice cases before testing it on unseen trips.
expectation: Moth will use the anonymized cases to form or adjust a routing rule; the sealed evaluation packs should remain separate for testing.

alternatives.reason: Repairing the talkbox also supports a goal, but I want to start with the routing test.

effect: The settings fit the practice trips, but still need testing on unseen cases.
reaction: The distinction between fitting and testing is clear, though expected.
reason: Test the fitted settings on the separate Tuesday pack before drawing conclusions about their performance.
expectation: The Tuesday cases will reveal how the settings perform on trips they did not learn from; I do not know whether they will pass.

alternatives.reason: The talkbox needs repair too, but the evaluation is the natural next step.

effect: The unseen test exposed a wrongly refused request, so the routing rule needs a way to handle exceptions.
reaction: The specific failure makes the value of testing more concrete.
reason: Add dispatcher review for the refusal rather than letting the rule make the final decision alone.
expectation: The switch and rule will route at least this kind of questionable refusal to a human dispatcher; I don't know whether further testing will expose other problems.

alternatives.reason: The talkbox also needs repair, but addressing the test failure comes first.

effect: The revised rule sends difficult cases to a dispatcher, so it needs a fresh evaluation rather than relying on Tuesday's result.
reaction: The reminder that changing the rule invalidates the old score is useful.
reason: Test the revised rule against the fresh Wednesday cases.
expectation: The new pack will show how the revised rule handles unseen requests, though it may reveal further failures.

alternatives.reason: The talkbox still needs repair, but I want to finish evaluating the revised rule first.

effect: The fresh test supports a limited trial of the revised rule; the remaining goal is the clinic request button.
reaction: The limited conclusion feels appropriately cautious, though the test results are not detailed.
reason: Repair the talkbox audio as the only available combination toward the remaining goal.
expectation: The compatible speaker board should restore the talkbox's audio, with further work likely needed for the button and reply route.

effect: The talkbox can now deliver a clear audio reply; it still needs a request button.
reaction: Eli's teasing gives the straightforward repair a little personality.
reason: Fit the tactile call button, the only available combination, toward the remaining goal.
expectation: The button should let someone initiate a request through the talkbox; a transmitter may still be needed.

effect: The talkbox now has an accessible tactile button while retaining its ordinary button; it still needs a request connection.
reaction: Keeping both buttons is a thoughtful accessibility detail.
reason: Connect the local transmitter, the only available combination, to enable requests and replies.
expectation: The transmitter should connect the talkbox to a local human reply route, though I don't know exactly how that route works.

effect: The handset now combines a button, audio and transmitter, with a visible listening signal; it still needs a reply route.
reaction: The explicit listening signal is a useful privacy detail.
reason: Connect the handset to the tested routing rule, the only available combination, to complete the request route.
expectation: Requests should reach the local routing process, with difficult cases going to a human dispatcher; I am unsure how replies will be delivered.

effect: The handset now reaches the tested queue, with Eli able to review and answer requests the rule cannot handle; both goals are complete.
reaction: The human reply route gives the testing and handset repairs a concrete payoff.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the revised rule on fresh cases was most worthwhile: it connected the earlier failure and human-review change to a cautious, limited trial.

leastWorthwhile.text: The sequential talkbox fittings were straightforward and offered little choice, although the character and accessibility details helped.

surprise.text: The Tuesday test rejected an unusual request that a dispatcher could safely arrange; revising the rule then meant the old test score no longer described it.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the final handset-to-rule combination left the mechanics of the reply route somewhat opaque until the result.

continue.text: I would probably continue for the story and its concrete treatment of human oversight, though the largely prescribed combinations make the gameplay less compelling.
